author: root

silhouette.reason: All twelve native poses read as a compact human with a broad cap/head, attached shoulders, dressed hips and shoe masses. Front head at y12-21 and torso/legs at y22-31 are balanced; front shoulder arms span x2-13 beneath the x1-14 head. Profiles keep bag mass behind the torso. Shape remains simpler and less expressive than the Emerald protagonists.

anatomy.reason: Cheeks narrow into a skin chin at y21 and a connected collar at y22; sleeve/hand clusters remain connected. Profile collar broadens under the chin without an exposed neck peg. Hip and upper-leg chains at y27-28 now bend and shift by phase, continuing to traceable shoes. The face and some cloth transitions remain intentionally geometric.

walking.reason: All directions exchange support and swing roles. Front stepA has left upper-leg bend at x3-5/y28 and the longer left shoe chain through y31; stepB mirrors the support depth with a right upper-leg bend. Back reverses those roles for its heading. Right stepA plants x10-13/y31 while the far shoe ends y30; stepB plants x3-6/y31 while the opposite shoe ends y30, with exchanged near/far trouser chains. Left mirrors this. Arm action opposes leg phase. Gait is restrained and fixed in head height rather than highly expressive.

pixelCraft.reason: Cap lights form connected clusters, the softened chin avoids a horizontal outline barrier, and the vest has continuous cream and blue planes through y23-26. Profile pack bulges at x2/y24-25 and tapers at x3/y26 instead of a straight pillar. Shoe and limb pixels remain attached. Dark contour and trouser shades are close, and some sleeve/face transitions retain visible geometric stepping, limiting craft score.

identity.reason: Front cap and blue vest with cream undershirt are coherent across phases. Back has a gold plane with brown side and red lower pocket. Profiles give the same pack a gold bulge, red pocket and lower brown corner behind the torso. Costume shape and accessory attachment are consistent, although material shaping and character specificity are simpler than official protagonist references.

directionContinuity.reason: All four headings retain the same head/body scale, red cap, blue vest, dark trousers/shoes and rear gold-red pack. The bag stays behind the profile torso and the two profiles follow the same mirrored lighting convention. No heading loses identity or scale.

loop.reason: Every decoded frame lasts 140ms and personally matches the intended native stepA-idle-stepB-idle sequence in each heading. Head stays fixed at y12; arm and leg changes are phase-related, not garment recolors or unexplained jumps. Final idle matches the first idle and returns to stepA without a data seam. Repeated neutral frames and restrained weight transfer give a deliberate simple cycle rather than the strongest motion nuance. Root-generated browser record and screenshot were inspected; no live playback observation is claimed.

reviewIndependence: Same-model organizational/task separation only; no different-model or decorrelated aesthetic independence is claimed.
nonblockingLimitations: Face and sleeve shaping remain more geometric and less expressive than the actual Emerald reference protagonists.
Contour and trouser darks have limited visual separation.
The fixed-height four-frame walk is deliberately restrained; repeated neutral phases limit motion nuance.
decisionReason: 85 meets the frozen threshold, every axis minimum and zero critical failures. Specific native evidence for shaped shoulder/chin/vest masses, a rounded rear profile bag, shifted upper-leg chains and genuine profile support exchange supports the result. Previous v14 scores and iteration count were not art anchors. Structural checks do not earn aesthetic points.
